question: What is a MOSFET?
answer: MOSFET is an electronic device most widely used in ICs.
reference_answer: A MOSFET is an electronic device most widely used in integrated circuits, with three terminals named source, drain, and gate, fabricated on a P-type semiconductor substrate.

sources.text: Let us discuss MOSFET in detail. MOSFET is an electronic device most widely used in ICs. It has three terminals named as source, drain and gate. The design of basic design of MOSFET is quite simple. Just take a block of P-type semiconductor. This block will be your base for MOSFET. We also call it as substrate and the entire MOSFET we will fabricate on this base. Now two portions on the same side of this P-type substrate are made highly doped with N-type impurity as these are shown here in the figure. Source and drain terminals are brought out from these two N regions are shown. Now the entire surface of the substrate is coated with a layer of silicon dioxide. Silicon dioxide will behave here as insulation. On this layer of silicon dioxide a thin metallic plate is placed. This metallic plate will act as gate contact to the substrate. The gate terminal is brought out from this metallic plate. Hence it is seen from the figure that gate contact is insulated from the substrate,

This metallic plate will act as gate contact to the substrate. The gate terminal is brought out from this metallic plate. Hence it is seen from the figure that gate contact is insulated from the substrate, but drain and source contacts are directly connected to respective N-type regions. This was the construction feature of a MOSFET. Now we will come to the operational features of MOSFET. For that we have to connect on DC voltage source between these two N-type regions. The N-type region connected with positive terminal of the source is called as drain, and the N-region connected with negative terminal of the source is called as source. As soon as the drain and source are connected with DC voltage source there will be two PN junctions formed. One is in between N-type drain and P-type base, and the other is in between P-type base and N-type source. As drain is connected with positive terminal of the source the drain is in higher voltage than base.

So, below threshold voltage, the device will behave as non conducting or in offboard. And for gate voltage greater than threshold value, the device will be in conducting or on mode. So this type of MOSFET is suitably used as a gate control switching device. Thank you.

More the applied voltage greater the width of the channel, means greater the conductance between drain and source. Here we have seen that there is no direct connection between gate contact and substrate. Instead, these are insulated from each other. But due to electrostatic attraction, the conducting channel between drain and source is formed, and because of that, the channel is also called induced channel, and the device is called induced channel MOSFET. It is also clear that when there is no voltage applied to the gate of the device, there will be no current from drain to source, except negligible amount of saturation current due to minority carriers. But if the gate voltage is gradually increased by keeping fixed drain to source voltage, after certain minimum applied gate voltage, drain to source current will start flowing. And this voltage is called threshold voltage. So, below threshold voltage, the device will behave as non conducting or in offboard.

question: How many terminals does the MOSFET described in the lecture have?
reference_answer: The MOSFET described in the lecture has three terminals: source, drain, and gate.

question: Why is the gate of a MOSFET insulated?
answer: The gate contact is insulated from the substrate, because silicon dioxide will behave as insulation.
reference_answer: Because the entire surface of the substrate is coated with silicon dioxide insulation, and the gate contact is placed on that insulated layer.

question: How does a MOSFET operate?
answer: After certain minimum applied gate voltage, drain to source current will start flowing.
reference_answer: A MOSFET operates by using gate voltage to induce a conducting channel between the drain and source; current flows only when the gate voltage exceeds the threshold voltage.

Now let us see what happens if one suitable positive voltage is applied at gate terminal of the device. In that case, due to attraction of positive potential of gate contact plate, negative free electrons that is minority carriers in P-type base will be accumulated towards a contact plate and form a channel of negative charge carriers, even inside P-type semiconductor. This channel due to higher concentration of free electrons will behave as N-type semiconductor, although entire base is doped with P-type or trivalent impurity. It is obvious that the number of free electrons accumulated towards gate contact plate depends on the strength of positive potential given to the gate terminal. Hence, width of N channel depends on the voltage applied at gate terminal. More the applied voltage greater the width of the channel, means greater the conductance between drain and source. question: What is the role of the drain and source terminals?
answer: The N-type region connected with positive terminal of the source is called as drain, and the N-region connected with negative terminal of the source is called as source.
reference_answer: The drain is connected to the positive side of the DC source and the source is connected to the negative side; they form the current path when the MOSFET turns on.
